newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel agriculture ministry says no to Cairo summit.
newsitem.headline: Israel agriculture ministry says no to Cairo summit.

text.p: Israel's agriculture ministry, following the example of the national infrastructure ministry, has suspended its plans to participate in a Middle East economic conference in Cairo, a spokesman said on Monday.

"The director-general gave the order to people in the ministry who intended to go to Egypt to stop all preparations because Egyptian chambers of commerce said they were ordering their members...to boycott Israel completely," ministry spokesman Naftali Yaniv told Reuters.
"So the director-general asked, 'Why should we go?' Yaniv said.
The spokesman said that unless Agriculture Minister Rafael Eitan reversed the order, the ministry's representatives would be staying home next week.

Like National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon, who said on Sunday no one from his ministry would attend the November 12-14 regional conference, Agriculture Minister Rafael Eitan is a former general and a vocal right-winger.
Sharon said he was keeping his people away from the conference because Egypt's political leaders and newspapers had been attacking the Israeli government.
Israel's delegation to the conference will be headed by Commerce and Industry Minister Natan Sharansky.

The Cairo meeting is the third annual regional development conference since Israel began peace negotiations with Palestinians, Syria, Jordan and Lebanon in 1991. Syria and Lebanon have boycotted the past two conferences and conditioned their attendance to a breakthrough in the bilateral talks.
Israel has since signed interim peace deals with the Palestinians and a peace treaty with Jordan. Egypt was the first Arab state to make peace with Israel, in 1979.

The conferences were originally aimed at integrating Israel into the region's economy. But a faltering peace process since the May election of right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has placed unexpected hurdles before the Cairo gathering. Many say Israel could find itself ignored by Arab businessmen at the meeting of 85 states.
